week_in_brief: Grocery marketers are navigating private label surges and retail media saturation as inflation-weary shoppers continue to trade down — and digital shelf visibility becomes more competitive than ever.

items.headline: Private label unit share reached 22.4% in Q1 2026 — the highest level since 2001 — squeezing national brand shelf presence
items.tag: 🏷️ PRIVATE LABEL | Store Brand Share Hits 25-Year High
items.whats_happening: Inflation fatigue is accelerating private label adoption across every grocery category. National brands are losing shelf position not just to private label products but to retailers actively reducing SKU counts to favor their own margins. The squeeze is particularly acute in pantry staples and frozen.
items.so_what: For CPG clients, this is a critical moment to invest in the digital shelf — if you're not winning on the retailer's search results page, you're invisible. National brand equity still matters in-store, but at the digital point of sale (Instacart, retailer apps, Walmart.com), search visibility is the new shelf placement.

items.headline: Instacart ROAS benchmarks fell to 3.2x in Q1 2026 from 4.8x in Q1 2025 as advertiser competition increases
items.tag: 📱 DIGITAL SHELF | Instacart Ads Efficiency Drops as Platform Matures
items.whats_happening: Instacart's advertising platform is maturing and pricing accordingly. As more CPG brands have shifted budget to the platform, auction competition has increased and returns have normalized. The early-mover advantage for grocery advertisers on Instacart is largely gone.
items.so_what: Instacart is still worth being on — but it requires more sophistication now. Keyword-level optimization, bid stratification by product velocity, and creative testing matter more than they did when the platform was new. Brands treating it as set-and-forget are seeing the worst returns.

items.headline: Grocers with high app engagement among loyalty members are seeing basket sizes 31% larger than non-app shoppers
items.tag: 🛒 LOYALTY | Grocery Apps Drive 31% Higher Basket Size Among Weekly Actives
items.whats_happening: App-engaged loyalty members — those who open the app at least weekly — are the highest-value grocery shoppers by virtually every measure: larger baskets, higher frequency, lower churn. Grocers investing in personalized in-app offers and push notifications are seeing outsized returns.
items.so_what: For grocery retail clients, this reframes the app not as a tech project but as a marketing channel. The ROI question isn't "what does the app cost to maintain?" — it's "what's the lifetime value gap between app-active and non-app loyalty members?" That's usually a compelling number.

this_weeks_take: Grocery marketing is getting harder on two fronts simultaneously: national brands are losing physical shelf presence to private label, and digital shelf competition is intensifying as more brands finally show up to platforms like Instacart. The opportunity is in the middle — brands that combine strong digital shelf discipline (search-optimized content, smart bidding, fresh creative) with loyalty and app engagement strategy are the ones who can weather the trade-down pressure. The brands treating digital as an afterthought are getting squeezed from every direction.
